regime: Risk-On Rotation (Bounce Under Resistance, Vol Easing)
summary: Friday's selloff got bought back Monday. NQ recovered 1.21 percent to close 29,744 and reclaimed its trend stop, and MES added 0.48 percent to 7,740. December gold gave back its safe-haven bid, slipping 0.63 percent to 4,160.2 and losing its stop, while crude held its trend above a rising stop after rolling to December. VIX eased 7.8 percent to 18.43. Both indexes still close under EMA50, so this is a bounce inside a broken trend.

event.name: No scheduled US release (budget and shutdown backdrop continues)
event.consensus: The federal data calendar stays thin against the budget and shutdown situation. Scheduled releases remain unreliable, so there is no firm data catalyst.
event.actual: No major US release drove the tape. Monday was a positioning and rotation session after Friday's selloff.
event.surprise: The rotation was the story. Money came back into stocks while the safe-haven gold bid came off, and VIX eased about 7.8 percent.
event.nqReaction: NQ opened firm, a narrow opening range broke down at 13:55 UTC and failed, then price ran to a 29,983 high before fading to close 29,744, up 1.21 percent and back above its stop but still under EMA50.
event.crossAsset: MES recovered to 7,740.25, up 0.48 percent and back above its stop. December gold fell 0.63 percent to 4,160.2 and lost its stop. December crude eased 0.85 percent to 98.23 but held above a rising stop. VIX 18.43, down 7.8 percent.

observe.note: No OBSERVE-lane signals today. GAP_NQ and TSMOM252LO_NQ sit outside the Net Alpha Pro curriculum and are tracked for research only.

risk.openRisk: NQ, MES and crude long-trends are on, but both indexes close under EMA50 and gold flipped short, so the reclaim is unconfirmed.
risk.note: The bounce reclaimed the NQ and MES stops, but both close under EMA50, gold flipped its stop down, and Friday's range was wide, so this is a one-day bounce inside a broken trend, not a confirmed turn. Keep size reduced until a clean trend re-establishes, meaning a hold above today's stops (MNQ 29,658, MES 7,724, crude 97.53) and a reclaim of EMA50 (MNQ 29,851, MES 7,758). Crude is the cleanest long, above a rising December stop, but mind the roll and do not read the expiring November print near 101 as the trend. Gold is below its stop and mean now, so the easy safe-haven long is off until it reclaims 4,190. VIX eased to 18.43 but stays elevated, so let the stops do the work. The data calendar stays thin with the shutdown backdrop, so treat any headline as the catalyst. Next policy event is the FOMC meeting Oct 27 to 28.

psychology: After a hard down day the urge is to keep selling every bounce. Monday paid the other side. Grade the level in front of you instead of trading Friday's fear. A reclaim off a flush can be real, but one green session that still closes under EMA50 is a bounce, so keep size honest and let price reclaim the mean before you trust a new trend. One more tell: when your hedge sells off as stocks rise, like gold did today, that is the hedge coming off, not a fresh short to chase.

fullReport.html:
OR High 29,806 | OR Low 29,719.5 | Width 86.5 pts (0.29%)

Break DOWN at 13:55 UTC at 29,711.25, but the down-break failed. Price reversed, ran to a 29,983 high above the range, then faded to close 29,744 back inside, below NYVWAP 29,809.7 and HOF VWAP 29,813.13.

It is Monday, so BIR skips the day. The back-in-range shape formed but was not an eligible play, HOF (short only) did not set up on a recovery, and nothing flagged a clean bounce for BNC.

The structure still tells you the flush got bought, even with the Monday filter keeping BIR on the bench.

Price closed 29,744, just below AVWAP inside the normal range. The day was a wide two-way swing: the 29,983 high tagged beyond the plus 3s band (exhaustion) before fading, and the 29,653 low reached the minus 2s to minus 3s zone. On a swing day like this the bands get hit both ways, so clean one-directional reversion entries were scarce, and the close back near AVWAP says the session ended roughly balanced.
